title: Rework span lifecycle and port runtime tracing to OTLP gRPC adapter
creator: Maya Patel
description: Background: our current runtime uses a mixture of legacy Jaeger/Thrift exporters and a homegrown span lifecycle that creates significant per-request allocations and contention under high QPS. This ticket replaces the custom exporter path with an OTLP gRPC adapter, reworks span object lifecycle to a pooled model, and refactors the batching/flush logic to use a bounded ring buffer and single-writer async flusher. Goals: reduce tail latency at 95/99 percentiles, lower CPU and GC overhead in the serving runtime, simplify exporter maintenance by standardizing on OTLP gRPC, and preserve trace fidelity (parent/child/span attributes) across goroutines/threads and async handlers.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing pipeline exports via OTLP gRPC adapter in production can be toggled per-deployment and matches existing trace shapes for 90% of sampled requests
End-to-end p95 latency for inference requests does not regress by more than 5% compared to baseline; p99 improves by >= 10% for the heavy-tail benchmark
Heap allocation per request reduced by >= 40% in the runtime benchmark (measured in benchmark harness), and GC pause percentiles improved
Span loss under sustained 10k RPS sampling rate < 0.1% with bounded memory under default config
No observable increase in error rates in canary deployment for 24 hours; rollback plan validated
Console and downstream observability services (trace linking, trace search) remain compatible; update docs and export mapping table
Design doc, migration guide, and at least one migration-runbook for Dedicated/Private are published and peer-reviewed
notes: Approach outline: (1) introduce otlp-grpc adapter shim that implements existing trace-shape contract, (2) implement a SpanPool to avoid per-span allocations, (3) replace current buffered channel batcher with a ring buffer + single background flusher guarded by atomic state, (4) add wire compression option (gzip) for high-throughput tenants, (5) expose runtime flags to toggle sampling heuristics and queue sizes

Trade-offs considered: pooling reduces allocations but increases complexity around reset/zeroing fields; we will require strict unit tests to prevent leaked references. OTLP gRPC simplifies exporter maintenance but can increase CPU for protobuf serialization — mitigated by batching + compression and by using protobuf preallocation pools.

Benchmarks: initial microbench shows 48% allocation reduction and 12% p99 latency improvement in synthetic KB sequence tests (internal benchmark dashboard link below). Need to run full e2e with realistic workloads (chat, long context).

Migration plan: feature-flagged rollout in three phases: dev-test -> canary region -> global. Fallback path keeps legacy exporter hot-swappable for 24h until next rollout phase. For Dedicated/Private customers, provide a toggle and documented migration steps.
Backward compatibility: otlp adapter will accept legacy tag mappings; we'll provide a one-off compatibility translation layer for a 2-week transition period after global rollout.
implementation_steps: Create otlp-grpc adapter package implementing current exporter interface
Implement SpanPool with lifecycle unit tests and race detector runs
Replace channel-based batcher with ring buffer and single-writer flusher; add flushing backpressure metrics
Add config knobs for batch size, flush interval, compression, and sampling heuristics
Integrate adapter with Console trace ingestion contract and add end-to-end tests
Run bench/soak test in staging and measure memory/latency improvements
Canary rollout and monitoring playbook, then global rollout with rollback steps
risks: Pool misuse causing data leakage — mitigated via aggressive unit/integration tests and code review
Increased CPU due to protobuf serialization — mitigated by batching/compression and profiling hot paths
Compatibility gaps for older Private deployments — mitigated by keeping legacy exporter togglable and providing migration docs
